subject: Verity PHI integration — model route lock & legal checklist
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@verityhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PHI workflow — request for route lock and no-fallback

Hi Jordan,

We're moving forward with the pilot that will route PHI-containing transcripts from our patient portal into your inference API. Per our compliance team, we need a strict routing commitment for those flows: requests must be served only from a vetted, US-residency-only model variant (no automatic fallback) and the traffic must be pinned to a dedicated cluster.

Requirements:
- No-fallback to non-residency or lower-tier variants
- Model pinned to 'redwood-phi-v1' (or equivalent approved variant)
- Data residency: US-only (us-east-1 preferred)
- Audit trail: request-level trace IDs for five-year retention

Timeline: pilot kicks off 2028-09-06. We need a signed mutual action plan + evidence of the routing controls before the pilot starts.

I'm attaching our security questionnaire and a short FAQ.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Senior Program Manager, Integrations
Verity Health Systems
Attachments: verity-security-questionnaire.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@verityhealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PHI workflow — request for route lock and no-fallback

Samantha — thanks for the clear note and timeline. Looping in Product, Infra and Legal to confirm feasibility and next steps.

High level response:
- We can support a US-residency-only pinned variant for PHI traffic on Dedicated or Private deployments; Hosted may need dedicated capacity.
- No-fallback is feasible but increases operational risk (loss of capacity = errors). We should define a fallback policy that returns an explicit error and a retry window instead of silently falling back.

Next asks for Verity:
1) Confirm whether you'll be on Dedicated or expect Redwood-hosted with reserved capacity.
2) Share the minimal success criteria for the pilot (latency SLO, throughput estimates, allowed error behavior).

I'm attaching a draft mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan-draft.xlsx) and will set a 30-minute sync for Friday.

—Jordan
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachments: mutual-action-plan-draft.xlsx

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@verityhealth.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PHI workflow — request for route lock and no-fallback

Thanks, Jordan. Quick product note on tradeoffs and options.

Option A (Recommended for pilot):
- Dedicated pool in us-east-1 pinned to approved model artifact (redwood-phi-v1).
- No automatic fallback. If the pool is unavailable, requests return 503 + structured error including trace ID.
- Canary rollout: start with a 1% traffic slice to validate performance and SLOs.

Impacts:
- Cost: + ~18% per token vs standard multi-tenant serving due to reserved capacity and isolation.
- Latency: slightly higher tail latency when pinned single-variant due to less instance pooling; we can mitigate with small prefix caching and warmup.

Acceptance criteria needed from Verity:
- Peak qps and average request size
- Maximum acceptable tail latency (p95/p99)
- Retry/backoff policy for client

I'll document the model-binding config and hand it to Dev.

—Grace
Senior Product Manager, Serving
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@verityhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Aug 2028 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PHI workflow — request for route lock and no-fallback

We can implement the route lock with these operational tasks:
- Provision dedicated capacity pool in us-east-1 and pin model artifact redwood-phi-v1.
- Add routing policy 'verity-phi-route' with strict no-fallback flag set.
- Emit request.trace_id and route.metadata to audit logs with retention 5 years (requires extended log retention addon).
- Add circuit-breaker that flips to 503 when capacity falls below threshold; this prevents silent fallback but does cause outages if capacity exhausted.

Config stub attached: route-lock-mvp-config.yaml
Notes:
- We'll need a one-hour maintenance window for initial provisioning and DNS cutover.
- Monitoring: set p95/p99 latency alarms and an incident runbook.

—Dev
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: route-lock-mvp-config.yaml

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <legal@verityhealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PHI workflow — request for route lock and no-fallback

Samantha / Verity legal — one quick legal checklist before we can sign the mutual action plan:
- BAA amendment (we'll prepare a draft). Need Verity's full legal entity name for the addendum.
- Explicit statement in MSA that no-fallback behavior is required for specific data flows and that Redwood's responsibility is to return 503s when capacity unavailable.
- Audit evidence: SOC2 report (latest) and confirmation of extended log retention (we'll provide a linkage to our compliance portal).

If you can confirm the legal entity and whether Verity requires Redwood-hosted Dedicated or customer-managed Private infra, we can finalize the DocuSign and aim to be signed by 2028-08-30.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: none
